videos.title: Winx Club: The Magic Is Back
videos.description: Regardez ce samedi 28 novembre sur BBC2 à 08:40 le programme "Winx Club: The Magic Is Back" produit en Italie en 2025. D'une durée de 25 min ce programme est adapté à tous publics.

videos.title: The Next Step: Cheer
videos.description: The Next Step's Kenzie salvages what is left of a broken cheer team, desperate to prove that she can bult this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for the nationals.

videos.title: Newsround
videos.description: Unique programme that provides children with all the latest news and current events from UK and around the globe, educating and informing them. Young viewers will have a chance to hear all the important stories, see the pictures and videos, and find out what is going on. This children's news programme also deals with various serious topics and sensitive issues that are affecting young people and the world.

videos.title: Blue Peter
videos.description: Longest running children's programme in the world, featuring current affairs, competitions, celebrity interviews, popular culture and 'do-it-yourself' instructions on creating arts and crafts trinkets from everyday household items. A multitude of presenters have hosted the show, joined in the studio by their pet dogs and cats, which have become firm favourites with family audiences. Young invitees who share their skills or stories of bravery win a coveted 'Blue Peter' badge, The show, which has a nautical title and theme tune, was launched in October 1958 by its first producer Biddy Baxter, an

videos.title: Gardeners' World
videos.description: Winter may be closing in, but Adam Frost has thrown on his warm coat and is sharing some practical jobs and seasonal inspiration to keep gardens thriving through the colder months. From planting shrubs and creating a striking winter container to laying a brick path, there's plenty to be getting on with in preparation for spring. In Hertfordshire, Ashley Edwards is given an exclusive tour of a stunning walled garden. Rachel de Thame reveals her secrets for growing spectacular dahlias, while Joe Swift discovers an extraordinary garden in Dorset bursting with beauty and inspiring plant combinatio

videos.title: Life in a Cottage Garden with Carol Klein
videos.description: Plantswoman Carol Klein shares with us a year in her garden at Glebe Cottage in north Devon. Carol has looked after her garden for over 30 years, each with its own rewards and delights, as well as problems and challenges. Follow Carol as her garden grows, flourishes, dies and is reborn. The first episode covers January and February. The frosts have not yet released their grip on the garden, and the devastation of a hard winter is scattered all around. There is much to do – cutting back, preparing the soil and planting garlic. The first green shoots of the year begin to appear as drifts of snow

videos.title: Naturewatch
videos.description: Nature is full of extraordinary surprises, and Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin are uncovering some of its more curious mysteries. Why do foxes' eyes shine in the dark? How did fish farts almost cause an international diplomatic incident? Does ivy really damage the trees it climbs? And how exactly do sea anemones deliver their sting? Together, they get to the bottom of these fascinating wildlife questions, with plenty of surprising discoveries along the way.

videos.title: Whisky Galore!
videos.description: Classic Ealing comedy about a whisky-laden ship that runs aground off the coast of the Outer Hebrides during the Second World War. The local islanders have depleted their supply of the amber nectar and are overjoyed at the thought of stocking up again. But it is Sunday, and the teetotallers object to making free with the unexpected cargo.

videos.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
videos.description: Marcus makes plans to expand the smallholding's herb patch. A trip to Gloucestershire to see the UK's largest herb collection shows that even someone as experienced as Marcus can still learn a lot about ingredients. Back at the smallholding, gardener Anatoli shows Marcus how to look after the bees and harvest the honey, and Marcus brings in some junior chefs to get inspired in the way the kitchen garden is inspiring him. Once the new herbs are in place, Marcus cooks up a herby feast for the people who have helped him along the way.

videos.title: Homes Under the Hammer
videos.description: A beautiful building in Bath. Martin meets a couple who have bought a flat in a period, listed building, and luckily for them, they own the flat below too. In West Yorkshire, Martel meets two pals hoping to turn four flats into six!

videos.title: Kelly's Heroes
videos.description: WWII France. When a German officer carrying some gold bars falls into the hands of a US platoon, Kelly and his sergeant Big Joe gather a team of men to "liberate" the remaining ingots, worth millions, from a bank behind enemy lines.

videos.title: Final Score
videos.description: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest news, analysis, reaction and interviews from the afternoon's biggest football matches.

videos.title: Snooker: UK Championship
videos.description: Follow the coverage of the prestigious international snooker tournament held in the UK every year since 1977.

videos.title: A Bridge Too Far
videos.description: The Allies have a daring plan to stop World War II by the end of 1944. Called Operation Market Garden, it involves parachuting 35,000 troops into occupied Holland to capture a strategic line of bridges. Could it work? Or are they going a bridge too far?

videos.title: U2 at the BBC
videos.description: A selection of U2's most memorable BBC appearances, including early songs such as their first Top 40 hit, Fire, on Top of the Pops in 1981; I Will Follow from a 1982 appearance on teen magazine show Something Else; and Two Hearts Beat as One from a rarely seen visit to The Kenny Everett Television Show in 1983. Other highlights include their 2011 set at Glastonbury – which featured classic tracks such as Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where the Streets Have No Name and Pride (In the Name of Love) – and a 2009 performance of Vertigo that wasn't just at the BBC, but on it, with the band singing from the

videos.title: U2: Live on the BBC at Tate Modern
videos.description: Global titans U2 perform at the Tate Modern in London for a truly unique live collaboration of music and art. Fifty years since the Dublin band formed at secondary school, the legendary four-piece return with their 16th album, Carnaval de Luz. For one night, they perform songs from the record and classic favourites, including Pride (In the Name of Love), Beautiful Day and With or Without You, visually accompanied by 77 Million Paintings, an artwork by producer, artist and long-time friend and collaborator of the band Brian Eno.

videos.description: Regardez ce dimanche 29 novembre sur BBC2 à 01:40 le programme "Snooker: UK Championship Extra" produit en Ecossais en 2026. D'une durée de 120 min ce programme est adapté à tous publics.

videos.title: Question Time
videos.description: Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Clydebank, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel, from the Scottish government, the economy, tourism and transport secretary Stephen Flynn; for Labour, the Scotland office minister Melanie Ward; the leader of the Scottish Conservatives Russell Findlay; the leader of Reform in Scotland Malcolm Offord; and Holly Bruce from the Scottish Greens. Watch or listen first on the BBC News Channel, iPlayer and Sounds at 9pm, or on BBC1 at 10.40pm.

videos.title: Honey
videos.description: When an old friend returns, Martha faces the danger of exposure, forcing her to confess all to Kurt and make a risky decision to trust him. They must both keep Kamilla onside, even whilst keeping secrets from her and one another. Fuelled by both his complicated entanglements with Martha and Kurt and an effort to outmanoeuvre her, Friedrich makes a drastic move to catch Martha out.

videos.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
videos.description: The county of Yorkshire is the setting for Christine Walkden's balloon tour of Britain. At Scampston Hall we discover two superstar garden designers and meet young gardener Nathan, who is just starting out. At York Gate Garden, Christine catches up with an old friend and we discover the Yorkshireman who was the father of aviation.

videos.title: Countryfile
videos.description: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

videos.title: BBC News
videos.description: The latest news from the BBC,which is designed to inform you on current affairs. The BBC is aims to be a totally impartial public service broadcaster, and was established by Royal Charter. The BBC is funded by a licence fee paid by British households, and is regulated by Ofcom. They aim to create high-quality content, in order to inform and educate, but also entertain, their audience Millions of people from all over the world watch content produced by the BBC, and they are well respected as a media company. It was founded in 1922, with its headquarters in Westminster, London.

videos.title: Landward
videos.description: Dougie is at Loch Tay in Perthshire, where he gets an insight into the lives or our Iron Age ancestors and visits a reconstructed crannog at a prime lochside location. Arlene is in the Carse of Gowrie to find out how the community won the right to buy and restore a historic orchard. Rosie is searching for Scottish truffles on the Isle of Bute, Shahbaz is in the Cowal Peninsula to meet the couple rewilding their dairy farm, and Anne is in Angus, where she meets the chocolatier using locally grown berries in her confectionery.

videos.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
videos.description: Matt Tebbutt delves into the archives to bring an array of delicious recipes from some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Alison Roman serves up her date and caramelised lemon pot roast chicken with a herb, garlic and pistachio salad. Owen Morgan brings along a taste of Spain, combining the flavours of mountain and sea for his chicken and seafood Spanish rice finished with a sherry and garlic aioli. Jamie Oliver takes to the hobs with an alternative to a traditional Christmas lunch: roasted venison loin wrapped in prosciutto, with a rustic celeriac mash finished with a chocolate and red wine sa

videos.title: White Christmas
videos.description: Two army buddies who have become entertainers travel to a Vermont ski resort for a well-earned rest. But on arrival, they find the resort, run by their old army commander, in need of a helping hand. There's only one answer – put on a show! Christmas classic with a memorable score by Irving Berlin.

videos.title: Snooker: UK Championship
videos.description: Follow the coverage of the prestigious international snooker tournament held in the UK every year since 1977.

videos.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
videos.description: Regardez ce dimanche 29 novembre sur BBC2 à 19:00 le programme "Celebrity Race Across the World" produit en Ecossais en 2026. D'une durée de 60 min ce programme est adapté à tous publics.

videos.title: Why Sinkholes Collapse
videos.description: On 24 September 2025, the main road outside one of Bangkok's major hospitals collapsed. The giant sinkhole, the size of two tennis courts, snapped water pipes, ripped down power lines, and swallowed two vehicles. During the day, it continued to grow, threatening the foundations of the hospital and forcing close to a thousand staff and patients to evacuate the building. Ampan Vimonvattana, vice dean of Vajira Hospital, witnessed the collapse: "The earth swallowed everything... it pulled the road surface, the soil, anything on top. Even the electrical poles got dragged down. It was really scary.

videos.title: Lucy Worsley's Keys to the Castle
videos.description: Lucy Worsley travels to Venice, where she is given the keys to the Doge's Palace, a multi-purpose building that controlled Venice's empire for a thousand years. She has a close shave in the dreaded Council of Ten's torture chamber, discovers a 24-carat gold staircase that leads to one of the biggest rooms in Europe, and encounters hidden doors and secret messages.

videos.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
videos.description: Paul and Bob are in Hampshire to fish both the River Beaulieu and the adjoining Solent. They're here to catch mullet and later take a boat trip up the Solent to try for a smooth hound. The Beaulieu is one of only a handful of rivers privately owned in the UK. It's been property of the Montagu family since the 18th century, and Paul and Bob have been given special permission to fish here. Later, they are joined by their doctor friend Anand Patel for an evening tipple and an update on their health. videos.title: A Course Called Ireland
videos.description: As their adventure nears its end, Bill still finds time to terrify Tom with his driving. A stormy round with NFL star Jason Kelce brings refuge in a stone shelter on the 7th, complete with pints and sausage rolls. In Dublin, Bill puts Tom in the spotlight for a change, before the pair reach the Giant's Causeway and reflect on a journey that became about far more than golf.

videos.title: Saving Private Ryan
videos.description: After surviving the carnage of D-Day, Captain Miller is ordered into heavily contested territory to find and return a single soldier. The mission proves to be both brutally dangerous and potentially pointless. Acclaimed Steven Spielberg World War II drama.

videos.title: The Misadventures of Romesh Ranganathan
videos.description: In the final part of his African odyssey, Romesh travels to the fourth largest island in the world – Madagascar. But like most people, when he brings to mind this former French colony in the Indian Ocean, his only reference is an animated Disney film. Romesh embarks on a mission, guided by exuberant diving instructor Bic, to find out what Madagascar has to offer the uninitiated – apart from cartoon dancing lemurs. videos.title: Lucy Worsley's Keys to the Castle
videos.description: Lucy Worsley has been given the keys to the spectacular palace of Versailles in France. The palace is huge – there are 2,000 rooms to explore, and everywhere Lucy discovers gold and more gold. This is one of the biggest and most ostentatious palaces she has ever seen. Lucy is here to find out more about France's most notorious queen, Marie Antoinette, who arrived at Versailles from Austria aged just 14 to marry the heir to the French throne. Her story is one of money, sex, power and snowy white goats.

videos.title: Blue Planet III
videos.description: A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time. videos.title: Match of the Day
videos.description: On a big Sunday of Premier League action, Arsenal face Manchester City, and it's Everton v Liverpool in the Merseyside derby. Brighton take on Newcastle, Crystal Palace play Hull City, Bournemouth go to Fulham, and Sunderland host Tottenham at the Stadium of Light. Presented by Gabby Logan.

videos.title: Politics Live
videos.description: Join presenter Jo Coburn as she discusses the latest political news and stories in a conversational format, covering the comings-and-goings from Westminster in the BBC's daily politics programme. Featuring opinions and arguments from all the sides of the political spectrum, the show invites informed and opinionated guests to share their views on the stories of the day. Andrew Neil presents a special edition of the show on Wednesdays, with live coverage of Prime Minister's Questions followed by analysis and reaction, dissecting all the important topics from the weekly House of Commons event.

videos.title: Flog It!
videos.description: This edition comes from Dover Castle in Kent, where antiques experts James Lewis and Catherine Southon search for items to take off to auction. James unearths a silver owl inkwell, and Catherine discovers an alabaster bust. Paul Martin delves into the history of the English Channel.

videos.title: House of Games
videos.description: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Matt Baker, Charley Marlowe, Rose Matafeo and Jack Rooke take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games skateboard?

videos.title: Strictly It Takes Two
videos.description: Ellie Taylor kicks off the week by exclusively chatting to the latest couple to be eliminated from the competition. Also, Friday's all-star panel of Strictly alumni return to break down all the weekend action from the ballroom.

videos.title: Global Eye
videos.description: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode, BBC Ukrainian Service reporter Anastasiya Gribanova sets out to uncover who killed her family. Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, her relatives, like countless others, were forced to confront painful questions of loyalty and identity. videos.title: Mastermind
videos.description: Four more contenders face the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Clive Myrie hosts and asks the questions on specialist subjects, which this time are King John, the 19th-century designer and artist William Morris, the musical Cabaret and the professional wrestler Bret Hart.

videos.title: Only Connect
videos.description: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. It's the third appearance of both teams, and a place in the next round is at stake. All they have to do is establish what connects a series of apparently random clues, such as ray, storey, underground storage and symbols of married status.

videos.description: Long-running general knowledge quiz that tests the intellectual powers of the brightest undergraduates in Britain. Launched in 1962 and hosted by Bamber Gascoigne, the show achieved cult status with teams from two different rival colleges pitting their wits against each other each week. The questions are as varied and as tough as they can be, and competitors risk having hard-earned points deducted with each incorrect response. Back in the cop car, Bert and Harry stay calm, while Stephen is terrified. It all comes to an unexpected end.
